.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 121 PM EST Tuesday...

1. Unsettled weather continues across the region today, with a 
period of drier weather expected tomorrow. 

2. Widespread precipitation looks likely Thursday into Friday, 
with some wet snow accumulations possible for the higher terrain, 
although exact impacts still need to be determined. 

3. Seasonably cool conditions with upslope showers this 
weekend, then trending drier into next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 121 PM EST Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The unsettled weather continues this afternoon as 
another shortwave moves through the region. The greatest chances for 
precipitation will be across the Adirondacks and northern Greens, 
particularly in the favored upslope locations. There may be enough 
instability to allow for a few heavier downpours or even some 
graupel, but for the most part light rainfall is expected with snow 
levels near summit level. Some of the upslope showers may linger 
into tomorrow morning, especially across the Northeast Kingdom, but 
overall tomorrow will feature drier weather ahead of the next system 
arriving late week. Temperatures to be rather seasonable through 
tomorrow, with daytime highs in the upper 30s to near 50 and 
overnight lows generally in the 30s.

KEY MESSAGE 2:  Confidence continues to increase in the likelihood of 
widespread precipitation across the region Thursday into Friday. A 
large scale upper level trough looks to build across the eastern 
CONUS, with surface low pressure centered in the Ohio Valley. As the 
initial low moves eastward, a secondary coastal low is expected to 
develop and strengthen, which will bring our chances for widespread 
precipitation. Although there is still some uncertainty regarding 
the exact timing and track of the system, it looks to be fairly 
progressive and consensus continues to grow amongst guidance as we 
get closer. Some of the biggest uncertainty has been and continues 
to be on expected precipitation type with this event. Higher 
elevations can expected to receive some wet snow accumulations with 
this event, but valley rain is expected for the most part, 
especially with the lack of cold air initially. Some snow may mix in 
at the lower elevations, particularly Thursday night into Friday 
morning, but accumulations are not expected. Another area of 
uncertainty is how quickly cold air advects into the region which 
could allow for some additional snowfall on the backside of the 
system, although there is still some uncertainty on amounts. As of 
now, snowfall totals look to be between 1-4 inches across the High 
Peaks of the Adirondacks and the spine of the Green Mountains 
Thursday and Friday. As previously mentioned, there is still some 
uncertainty, so while confidence has increased there are still some 
details that change over the next day or so. Temperatures are expect 
to trend cooler towards the end of the week, with highs generally in 
the 30s to low 40s by Friday.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Upper level troughing will prevail for much of the 
weekend, leading to a mostly cloudy and cool stretch. Friday night, 
surface low pressure will be tracking northeastward across the 
Atlantic, resulting in northwesterly flow for northern New York and 
Vermont and potential for upslope showers, 30-65% chance 
precipitation Friday night and Saturday. As temperatures fall from 
the 30s at the start of Friday to the seasonably cold upper 
teens/20s by early Saturday morning, any potential precipitation 
would start as snow at higher elevations, while wider valleys would 
see rain become rain/snow mix or even snow as temperatures fall 
their lowest. Showers may linger into Sunday at higher elevations, 
likely drying out by Monday. Snow levels rise again each day as 
highs reach a seasonably cool mid 30s and 40s, but are expected to 
fall each night to around 1000 feet or even lower as temperatures 
dip into the upper teens to lower 30s. Several inches will be 
possible in the mountains, but anything in the valleys would likely 
be lighter and have a hard time accumulating. Heading into next 
week, a large surface high pressure looks to build into the region, 
bringing increasing sunshine and cold overnight lows.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 18Z Wednesday...An unsettled weather pattern continues this
afternoon with showers likely, before drier weather returns
Wednesday. Current ceilings run anywhere from 1,300-10,000 feet
above ground level, with a scattered layer of clouds hovering around
1,000-1,200 feet and southerly winds gusting 10-25 knots at times.
Ceilings are expected to continue lifting throughout the afternoon,
leading to widespread VFR conditions by around 20Z-21Z today, but
for the mountain sites (SLK, MPV, and EFK), this could be brief
before heading back down to MVFR cigs for a few hours. As mentioned,
some showers are expected throughout the afternoon as well, and
visibility restrictions should be around 4-6 miles in showers,
though any heavier shower could bring vis lower. Shower threat is
expected to come to an end by 00Z- 06Z Wednesday. Gusty winds will
also continue through this time, turning more northwesterly
throughout the evening and overnight. A northwesterly low level jet
will be present overnight tonight, resulting in some potential brief
LLWS from 00Z-06Z before surface winds turn northwesterly to match
the upper levels.

Outlook...

Wednesday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA, Slight chance SHSN.
Thursday: Mainly IFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance RA, Chance
SN.
Thursday Night: IFR. Chance RA, Chance SN.
Friday: IFR. Chance RA, Chance SN.
Friday Night: Mainly IFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SN,
Chance RA.

SN.
Saturday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance RA,
Chance SN.
Sunday: Mainly MVFR, with local VFR possible. Slight chance RA,
Slight chance SN.
